17 Airspace Map Illustration Credits: MavDrones Credits: Xenox Note: While the airspace map provides a clear definition of zones, remote pilots must account for
unforeseen restrictions, such as Temporary Red Zones, that may arise in their operational
airspace. Given the dynamic nature of airspace regulations, the Remote Pilot in Command (RPIC)
bears full responsibility for ensuring compliance when operating a drone in such areas. It is
essential to reconfirm the classification of your airspace zone at the time of operation.
The DigitalSky Platform offers the functionality to upload flight plans and seek necessary
permissions for drone operations. Obtaining your Flight Authorization Number after uploading
your flight plan is strongly recommended. Additionally, it is advisable to inform local law
enforcement about your drone operation, especially if it is for commercial purposes. Even for
recreational flights, notifying law enforcement is a good practice when operating within regulated
